rites.name: Raulor
rites.text: A sacred tradition of twin-blessed rites grants a people a venom-tipped edge against foes. Scouts and skirmishers also gain the power to vanish within certain lands.

rites.name: Amisus
rites.text: A sacred civic principle in which a people calls down rains to restore the land. It is set in motion by the rites of a rain-giving power.

rites.name: Reniantum
rites.text: A tribal custom that spreads dread among neighboring warriors. Enemy fighters standing close by grow weaker in their strikes.

rites.name: Vintelus
rites.text: A sacred chant once sung by an early empire's priests during rites. It was built from fragments gathered from scattered recordings and reworked into a single melody.

rites.name: Lasum
rites.text: A sacred song or ritual piece that stirs the people nearby. It grants a small bonus to those standing beside those who perform it.

rites.name: Nilanum Amestum
rites.text: A ceremonial office held by a wise leader who guides a people's spiritual and civic life. Mastering its deeper teachings grants an extra sacred bond to a learned discipline.

rites.name: Caullantor
rites.text: A coastal blessing that lifts the spirits of a people living by the shore. Settlements gain added standing when they are built on or beside the water's edge.

rites.name: Niarium
rites.text: A martial discipline that lets fighters enter a fierce battle stance, greatly multiplying their strength, but bars them from ever withdrawing once the fighting has begun. It fades from use once sacred faiths take hold.

rites.name: Nilium
rites.text: A tradition held by a seafaring folk that strengthens their ability to win over independent peoples in faraway lands. It shapes how they forge alliances beyond their own shores.

rites.name: Tiarnenia
rites.text: A worker kneels and sets a stand of young trees onto the tile beneath them. Once planted, the tile becomes a woodland that stands where bare ground once lay.

rites.name: Telirnia
rites.text: A civic bond shared by the citizens of a young council-run realm, strengthening the mood of those who live under it. Its warmth grows stronger when the people are glad, and stronger still when they are overjoyed.

rites.name: Siastia
rites.text: A tribal ceremonial melody that accompanies a sacred dance held under the open sky. It is sung by a people who honor the sun and their ancestors.

rites.name: Millorum
rites.text: A tradition of learning practiced in the early kingdoms. It grants a small bonus to the places that sit beside certain other holdings.

rites.name: Vintiasus
rites.text: A custom of welcoming outsiders into a community as guests and allies. It makes the work of forging friendships with independent peoples go faster.

rites.name: Sialum
rites.text: A stirring of the realm's lesser lords that breaks out when a crisis overwhelms the ruling house. It weakens the walls of a settlement that has none.

rites.name: Amirnus
rites.text: Amirnus is a concept of Crede, the principle of a sworn oath made binding across the Courts during the Age of Sundering. In the trials of the second era, the concept was invoked to hold the doors between worlds shut when landfall split the old bonds apart.

rites.name: Valania
rites.text: A laborer uses this practice to scour away blight or a scar from the tile where they stand. It restores the ground to its former state.

rites.name: Oristenes
rites.text: A short sung refrain carried between temple courts and river barges, its phrases borrowed from older ceremonial hymns. It rises at dawn gatherings and marks the start of formal rites.

rites.name: Nintor
rites.text: A sacred rite that stirs the faithful during times of religious upheaval. Those who serve as wandering preachers within the realm become more persuasive and effective in spreading their teachings.

rites.name: Orisus
rites.text: A ravenous hunger that a sworn horde of the undead can be granted at the lowest rank of their war-training. It sharpens their pursuit of living flesh.

rites.name: Coriarnanum
rites.text: A grand doctrine of martial strategy practiced by an ancient eastern people, granting their warriors cunning advantages in battle. It is also recorded as a scenario that tests a ruler's skill in the field.

rites.name: Nantaurum
rites.text: A tier three discipline that lets defenders against mounted riders hold a tight formation. It can only be learned after the foundational shield-wall training is mastered.

rites.name: Siarnes
rites.text: A bold seizing practice where an armed force takes command of helpless carriers left without guard. Seized builders labor more slowly yet cost their captors nothing to sustain.

rites.name: Tiarnes
rites.text: A tier-three training rite that sharpens the charge of armored mounted warriors. Only riders who have first mastered a prior battle discipline may learn it.

rites.name: Coriarum
rites.text: A sacred dance that draws strength from the cold northern lands. Each frozen plain bordering a holy grove adds a little more blessing to its shrine.

rites.name: Coroseollus
rites.text: A practice in which a figure spreads a rumor within a chosen settlement, sowing discontent among its people. It works reliably on the careless and only sometimes on the watchful, and it demands a substantial sum to carry out.

rites.name: Vianaullor
rites.text: A disciplined warrior creed that becomes available only after a chosen study is completed. It grants a small bonus to each unit and gives troops a veteran training status at no cost.

rites.name: Mestia
rites.text: A disciplined fighting art taught to monks of the temple orders. It is unlocked after mastering one of two earlier training paths.

rites.name: Corinus
rites.text: A divine boon that speeds the mending of wounded warriors within sacred precincts and the ground bordering them, even for those who have marched that turn.

rites.name: Talium
rites.text: A covert craft of silent movement and hidden tactics, practiced in the wilds by those who prefer to strike unseen.

rites.name: Seolus
rites.text: A sacred devotion that grants a fifteen percent boost to the raising of great monuments during the earliest ages of a people. It belongs to the shrine traditions of ancient builders.

rites.name: Carialus
rites.text: A second-rank training distinction taught to fighting monks of a sacred order. It is earned only after a pupil has mastered one of two prior disciplines of stealth or shadow.

rites.name: Valausanus
rites.text: A tactic where warriors strike an enemy from the side rather than head on. It grants a bonus to the attackers in battle.

rites.name: Ameones Telaunus
rites.text: Devout healers in a temple order channel their devotion into restorative rites. Townsfolk who receive the cure hand over coin, which flows into the order's treasury.

rites.name: Cantostia
rites.text: A soldier halts in place and braces to strengthen its guard. Any step forward breaks the stance, while troops resting inside a stronghold add to its protection.

rites.name: Careolles
rites.text: A faith of the dunes grants its temples extra sacred strength for each neighboring tract of sand. Its devotees gain power from the barren ground that surrounds their shrines.

rites.name: Lianoses
rites.text: This body of hidden teaching lets its adherents raise a seer-hall that doubles the power of shrines. It also serves as the foundation for star-reading and reasoned inquiry.

rites.name: Teontonor
rites.text: A solemn chant sung at sacred gatherings and festivals, drawn from an older hymn. It carries the spirit of a ruler's ceremonial theme.

rites.name: Orosiallium
rites.text: A stately chant carried by a crowned ruler of an old realm, drawn from a prayer begging a higher power to hasten and help. It is sung during his march.

rites.name: Oranes
rites.text: A courtly art of subtle negotiation that lets a people advance through persuasion rather than force. It is practiced within the scenario-specific tradition of Oranes's assemblies.

rites.name: Orantium Tenaullia
rites.text: A joined power that awakens when two sacred sites are raised upon the same ground. It grants bonuses to the people who hold that ground.

rites.name: Telarornus
rites.text: A martial faith held by a people who follow it. Victories in battle grant spiritual strength equal to half the fighting power of the defeated foe.

rites.name: Serironus
rites.text: A first-rank technique taught to the wandering monks of a temple order, letting a fighter strike from the cover of gloom. It marks the lowest rung of a monk's training.

rites.name: Veollanum
rites.text: A devout mark of rank that a missionary-minded holy figure carries into the field. It lets the bearer spread a faith to new communities, drawn from a sacred scenario path.

rites.name: Ciasinum
rites.text: A rank of military training that a fighter gains after first mastering a lower-tier skill. It is unlocked only after one of two prerequisite disciplines has been learned.

rites.name: Lilastium
rites.text: A sacred rite pursued through a set number of shrines, granting its adherents spiritual insight and easier construction of holy halls.

rites.name: Ciallonanum
rites.text: A learned rank earned by a teacher-mystic on the road to enlightenment. It depends on first attaining a lesser guiding rank.

rites.name: Valasinanum
rites.text: A devotional rite that a wandering preacher may learn once a certain water-walking discipline has been mastered. It spreads the teaching of the faith to new listeners.

rites.name: Rantornium
rites.text: A keeper works on a settlement's outer walls, but only when they are broken and no raid has struck within the last three days. Each day of labor adds strength to the stonework until it is fully restored.

rites.name: Ciantus Ameolus
rites.text: A ruinous craft by which raiders strip a settlement of its goods and wealth. It is taught as a method for conquerors who seize what their enemies hold.

rites.name: Nastaures
rites.text: A third-tier vow of an ordered faith that rewards those who push past the sky. Followers of this creed gain a boost from daring ventures beyond the world.

rites.name: Veonausor
rites.text: A ceremonial melody performed by the island people during the rising of new harvests. It was recomposed by an outsider who drew on an older hymn from a distant temple school.

rites.name: Niarnorus
rites.text: A ceremonial doctrine that can be adopted only after a prior study is completed. It grants added favor to a people's craft and to scenic, awe-inspiring sites.

rites.name: Viantium
rites.text: A discipline of shared study and contemplative practice among wandering mendicants. Its members gather strength from their brotherhood and sharpen their skills through communal devotion.

rites.name: Riaseollus
rites.text: A tier-three discipline taught to a monk-warrior who has already mastered earlier training. It can only be unlocked after one of two prerequisite arts is learned.

rites.name: Oreriantus
rites.text: A rank of skill granted to archers and similar long-range fighters after they master a lower training tier. It requires first learning one of two prerequisite volleys or fire tactics.

rites.name: Orenium
rites.text: A practice in which scouts roam across a land to survey its terrain and hidden ground. Careful watching of the land shapes how a commander plans each move.

rites.name: Nistellia
rites.text: A devotional belief that grants a small bonus to mines dug over precious goods. Its followers carve sacred figures that bless the work of the deep pits.

rites.name: Canaurnium
rites.text: A devotional pact that quickens how far a people's holdings reach outward into new lands. Its keepers can also gain a free wanderer to found a fresh settlement.

rites.name: Naullia
rites.text: A sacred custom in which captured foes are turned into a surge of communal renown. This rite becomes a main path for a people to win by cultural glory.

rites.name: Amianum Cillernium
rites.text: A devoted agent may sell pardons to a rival holding, siphoning away its wealth and delivering it to the seller's own people. The act never fails and costs nothing to perform.

rites.name: Valistia Taules
rites.text: A seer's practice of casting dread over a chosen target, sowing unease in those it touches. The rite never fails, but it demands a heavy offering of wealth.

rites.name: Valeres
rites.text: A ritual promotion that lets a holy figure carry messages between peoples who share no tongue. Its bearer gains the skill to bridge speech across temples and courts.

rites.name: Vanor
rites.text: A learned instruction for a spiritual leader who guides others along a inner path. It is a skill that a practitioner gains and passes on to followers.

rites.name: Serintes Coreolus
rites.text: A wandering promotion earned by a holy envoy who journeys between settlements to spread teachings. It grants the envoy a boost tied to moving across the land.

rites.name: Tiarum Amelanum
rites.text: A first-rank training gift that a monastic fighter may claim, granting a measure of the discipline that lets them move unseen at dusk.

rites.name: Tirnes Veniallium
rites.text: A tier-one training discipline that sharpens fighters against mounted warriors. It grants a bonus for those who learn it.

rites.name: Serausum Naustor
rites.text: A consecrated rite that a sanctified shrine can perform to bring the restless dead within its borders under the caster's command for a fixed span of time.

rites.name: Amistanum
rites.text: A sacred war-fervor kindled in a people's temples that stirs every settlement on the shared landmass to bolster its defenses and muster greater hosts. It can rouse a ruler's warriors even without a commander at their head.

rites.name: Seranor
rites.text: A stately chant that a wandering people sing to mark their presence. It is shaped by the ballads of distant travelers met along old caravan roads.

rites.name: Aminia Rollanum
rites.text: A devotional technique that lets a holy wanderer cross open water as though it were solid ground. It is practiced by lone pilgrims on the road to enlightenment.

rites.name: Teleosor Telosaunus
rites.text: A sacred discipline followed by a theocratic people, granting its devotees a modest boost to their faith. Its adherents gain small bonuses from walking its path.

rites.name: Niastilum Corausanum
rites.text: A soldier may pull back from a losing clash and survive it. This lets an attacking warrior escape destruction rather than fall where it fought.

rites.name: Corollium
rites.text: A quiet practice that spreads calm through every settlement, lifting the spirits of all who dwell there. Its benefit fades once strange ancient discoveries reshape the world's knowledge.

rites.name: Coriastum
rites.text: A healing craft practiced by travelers and wardens that lets soldiers recover their strength even while camped among hostile lands. It is a wonder of the medieval age.

rites.name: Coraullus
rites.text: A forceful advance where a warrior pushes into an enemy's square, provided enough strength remains to reach it. Ground and naval forces must halt afterward, while winged forces may strike once and keep moving.

rites.name: Amostellium
rites.text: A covert skill for quietly ending a rival leader's life. Its study belongs to the sundered medieval age and is tied to courtly intrigue.

rites.name: Corestia
rites.text: A standing command that hardens a unit's guard, though the unit must stay fixed in place. Such a guarded soldier draws more blows from enemies, and certain ranged and pike-bearing fighters excel at this stance.

rites.name: Leostum
rites.text: A ruler's hold on the armies determines whether they rest in reserve with diminished vigor or rise to alert and war with restored strength. This stance also governs how swiftly the troops are healed and forged.

rites.name: Sereontium
rites.text: A victor may spare a beaten foe and bind it to their own side instead of slaying it. A chance applies after each win, and a captured fighter is transformed into another kind of unit and obeys its captor at once.

rites.name: Siarellum
rites.text: A crisis-time doctrine that stirs a community's devotion when faith is contested. It weakens the standing of rival believers while sharpening the efforts of those sent to spread the teachings.

rites.name: Maunistia
rites.text: Soldiers who have won fights gain a rank that makes them stronger when they strike first. Their assault power rises by half once this seasoning is earned.

rites.name: Meornosus
rites.text: A rule of pressure in which a force's presence restricts the movement of foreign troops standing close to it. The precise workings of this restraint differ from one realm to another.

rites.name: Crordock
rites.text: Crordock is the concept of the Fall of Crede, the moment the Sundering split worlds into Shards and the Pact was sworn over the broken ground. It names the bargain that let the first sovereign hold grove and kingdom together against the drifting fragments. Its force is that of a single bound oath rather than open war.

rites.name: Nases
rites.text: A fourth-rank combat technique for elite fighting monks, unlocked after mastering either of two earlier forms. It is taught to those who have already learned their discipline's lesser strikes.

rites.name: Ameosternus
rites.text: A learned method for reading the night sky that opens once seafaring knowledge is mastered. It grants a bonus to a people's wisdom and two free purchases of a sacred altar.

rites.name: Seostolia
rites.text: A tiered mark of a leader's magnetic appeal that grows a ruler's standing among their people. Its effects are strengthened in the cities and lands the ruler governs.

rites.name: Teleones
rites.text: A sudden flash of understanding that speeds a people's progress along their knowledge paths. Two forms exist: one quickens discovery of new techniques, the other quickens the growth of social ideas.

rites.name: Oriastia
rites.text: A leader's gift that binds the people of each settlement to them more firmly, while their soldiers rise through the ranks more quickly. It is honored through the raising of grand halls and signal towers.

rites.name: Nausintium
rites.text: A shared disposition that certain founders carry, making them inclined to work alongside others. Several leaders of one settling people are said to hold it.

rites.name: Coraurus
rites.text: A tactic where certain war engines strike several defenders gathered together in one group at once. Practitioners often shorten its label to a single slang word.

rites.name: Vastinium
rites.text: A ranked wisdom-token that can be invoked on a chosen tile to lift a nearby effort by three. Its use is tied to a particular placement.

rites.name: Rorantium
rites.text: A covert art by which agents turn a rival settlement's loyalty toward their own people, siphoning a share of its wealth. Success is likelier for those who preach on the air, and the act costs a sum of coin.

rites.name: Minum
rites.text: A tactic lets sea raiders climb onto enemy hulls to seize them. It is the first step in a raider's training along the coast.

rites.name: Raurneones
rites.text: A sudden burst of cultural force that instantly spreads a people's holdings into nearby unclaimed lands and even across rival borders. It is the only way to seize such territory without war or bargaining.

rites.name: Amintium
rites.text: A costly tactic where a unit siphons half of a rival's output and moves it to its own side. It can also be used to pull a foe out of a settlement, succeeding three times in four.

rites.name: Orentor
rites.text: A harsh decree that calls down a wrathful judgment upon a people. Those who follow its path are marked, and their faithful gain a measure of strength.

rites.name: Raurastia
rites.text: A binding legal writ that a trader can lodge against a rival town, halting its workshops from making or finishing any goods for one cycle. Advocates reliably win such writs, for a fee.

rites.name: Coresirus
rites.text: A short-lived ruling craft that lets a leader overturn established authority from below. It grants a sizable boost to output, though every affected holding carries an added upkeep cost.

rites.name: Veosanum
rites.text: A civic-level craft of sending wayfarers into uncharted lands to reveal what lies beyond the known horizon. Scouts sent out this way lift the veil of unknown terrain from the map.

rites.name: Vaustum
rites.text: A ruler may quietly push an unwanted foreign band out of their lands without striking it, so no harm is done and rivals are not provoked. The removed group is simply escorted to the closest allied stronghold.

rites.name: Caules
rites.text: A healing doctrine that becomes available during a wasting sickness. Its followers gain a reward when healers tend the afflicted within a dedicated infirmary.

rites.name: Tosanum
rites.text: A craft of reshaping living blood-lines that lets its masters raise a great healing works. The works grants a small joy to every settlement across the world for whoever holds it.

rites.name: Vonanum
rites.text: A covert art of gathering hidden knowledge through secret agents and cunning. It recurs as a method practiced across many rival realms in the wider world.

rites.name: Lauriasia
rites.text: A craft by which a winged vessel that lands on a supply station or a settlement with a fuel depot is replenished by the following turn. Replenishing restores its full distance of travel.

rites.name: Rania
rites.text: A quiet faculty possessed by every wayfarer and warband, letting each one perceive the goings-on across neighboring ground. It is a shared trait of all such bearers.

rites.name: Seorium Teliles
rites.text: A legal maneuver used by a counselor-type figure against rival trading agents, destroying them outright. It can also strip a merchant holding from a city, and it always succeeds for a steep fee.

rites.name: Telisontor
rites.text: A tactical doctrine that boosts gathered yields and plunder for its bearer. It also sharpens the bearer's standing with rival peoples once enough of its marks are displayed.

rites.name: Oreorianes
rites.text: A tactic in which a far stronger fighter crushes a weaker foe outright, ending the clash at once. The needed power gap is wider against wild raiders and narrower for one favored people.

rites.name: Ameostor
rites.text: A tide-touched craft that grows stronger beside flowing waterways and gains further strength from each dependent people under its command.

rites.name: Seornanum
rites.text: A tiered battle discipline for ships that fire from a distance. It must first be mastered through the earlier bombardment training.

rites.name: Lisaunia
rites.text: A tactical training that lets sea gunners fire at their enemies more effectively. It is taught after a prerequisite discipline is mastered.

rites.name: Contirnium
rites.text: A battlefield refinement that lets siege engines spray scattered fragments onto nearby foes. Each siege crew must first master a prior tactic before gaining it.

rites.name: Rostaunium
rites.text: A stealth discipline that lets sea raiders slip past notice, earned after mastering guided undersea munitions. It sits at the third rung of a warship's training ladder.

rites.name: Corenus
rites.text: A dormant state that lets a bearer's companions fall still and inactive for a while. Such companions are passed over when cycling through the group, and they rouse once a foe steps into a neighboring space.

rites.name: Amiasus
rites.text: Covert agents slip into a rival settlement to pilfer another people's learned craft. Attempts can fail, and the thief may be caught and slain, with a narrower chance of success when a specific craft is targeted.

rites.name: Veostanum
rites.text: A practice by which a worker restores a damaged construction back to working condition. It is treated as a task, a rank of skill, and an undertaking that may be carried out.

rites.name: Tolor
rites.text: A tactic of raiding for spoils during a period of early exploration. Foot soldiers and horsemen grow stronger against enemy troops when a band keeps enough such tactics displayed openly.

rites.name: Tornellia
rites.text: A covert practice of watching rivals from afar. It is trained into agents who use it to gather hidden knowledge.

rites.name: Mentia
rites.text: A learned craft passed between masters and apprentices in a river-town. It grants a small bonus of insight to those who study it under a guild of teachers.

rites.name: Tisialles
rites.text: A tide-driven craft of the sea-faring folk that spreads learning through voyages. It opens new paths of trade and knowledge for those who master it.

rites.name: Tentarsaum
rites.text: Tentarsaum is a concept of the Walled Age in Crede, a principle of holding back what would otherwise overrun the city wards, carried by the orders and churches of the Holy Age. Its adherents treat a wall as a living vow and kindle temple flames to renew the strength of the stone.

rites.name: Oraures
rites.text: A researcher-driven method that reads and reshapes the hidden structural code of native living things. It arose after early contacts with a world's awareness sparked wide excitement among scholars.

rites.name: Serasiarium
rites.text: A craft of hidden maneuvering in which a faction gains advantage by controlling secrecy itself. Practitioners treat concealment as a scarce resource to be hoarded.

rites.name: Vesus
rites.text: A special ability that lets a unit hold command of the open skies. Units bearing it gain an edge when contesting airborne ground.

rites.name: Valores
rites.text: A tactic that lets bomber craft in the second rank of training strike ground targets more effectively. It can only be learned once a craft has first mastered a formation drill or an evasion method.

rites.name: Oraunes
rites.text: A people's lasting special gift grants unique advantages that ease certain paths to triumph. Each one begins at the outset and new ones awaken as the realm's knowledge advances through its ages.

rites.name: Ventanum Vaurnium
rites.text: A mature policy that lets a people share its artistic heritage with distant peoples. Those who receive it gain a fresh measure of the giver's cultural pull.

rites.name: Ciria
rites.text: A tiered aerial discipline granted to bomber units, marking the first rank of advancement for airborne strike squadrons.

rites.name: Noleosanum
rites.text: A ritual project reserved for a clandestine circle of void-chanters. Once a sealed tower of carved idols stands and the chant is mastered, a city's yield is bent toward the rite, and its completion makes the circle's hidden followers far more able to sow unrest.

rites.name: Tilles
rites.text: A worker lays down a landing strip for flying craft on the tile it stands upon. This action lets the builder raise an aerodrome where it currently is.

rites.name: Amesia
rites.text: A solemn chant that opens a grand introductory recording, sung in an ancient tongue. Its words are drawn from an old hymn of warning to all peoples.

rites.name: Valerium
rites.text: A tradition that grants bonus output to tiles beside still inland waters. It is rooted in a shared cultural custom from the exploration era.

rites.name: Amauntor
rites.text: A covert card of deceit that a ruling council may slot into a wild position, spreading false word across the realm. It is open to councils from the age of broadcast until the far age of stars.

rites.name: Amaurnus
rites.text: A tuned surge of volume-driven spirit that a musical company can call upon to lift its performers beyond their usual limits. It is a rousing boost tied to the traveling bards of a modern age.

rites.name: Teontium
rites.text: A flashy stage-style bonus that a traveling musician band can earn to raise their performance. It is granted during a late-era cultural tour.

rites.name: Sereollia
rites.text: A ritual project that calls a legendary champion to a settlement once a central monument has been raised. Each champion has a dedicated rite, and a town can host only one of them as its guardian.

rites.name: Naustor
rites.text: A tradition that grants bonuses to units stationed beside a lake and a smaller boost to units traveling by water. It is practiced during the exploration age.

rites.name: Orialestes
rites.text: A hidden blight that a saboteur can loose upon a settlement, wiping out every unit within it. Neighboring towns that trade with the stricken place risk catching the contagion in the following turn.

rites.name: Rellontor
rites.text: Two paired combat boons granted when allied units cluster on neighboring squares, either to pin a foe from several sides or to shield one another while defending. Stacked carefully, these boons can swing a battle's outcome.

rites.name: Valolaustum
rites.text: A modern craft that grants a bonus to those who practice it beside still inland water. It also strengthens travelers who cross rivers or seas by boat.

rites.name: Serialontor
rites.text: A tier one training refinement given to airborne bombers that sharpens their ability to dodge incoming threats. It is the first tier of this line of aerial skills.

rites.name: Cerium
rites.text: A basic close-combat technique for the winged fighters of the realm. Pilots gain it early in their training, giving their flying warriors a first measure of skill in aerial battle.

rites.name: Menum
rites.text: A coined maneuver where a unit descends onto a distant target by dropping from a carrier vehicle. The descent may only begin from a designated transport or carrier source.

rites.name: Lianes
rites.text: A controlled campaign of messaging that bends how a populace thinks and feels. It raises the stance of the realm's people while stirring suspicion toward rival nations.

rites.name: Orosinor
rites.text: A covert tactic that a secret agent can learn to grow more skilled at spreading damaging rumors against rival rulers.

rites.name: Telorintum
rites.text: A specialized discipline of living-tissue craft that uses engineered contagions to carry changes into a body's inner code. Its gentle uses can heal, but hardened war-minded scholars can bend the same method into a devastating arm.

rites.name: Rellium
rites.text: A ruling art that can only be assembled by fusing ancient relic-stones together. It quickens the gathering of civic virtues across the realm by a fifth.

rites.name: Rostanum Reornium
rites.text: A practice in which one people take in the symbols and customs of another and weave them into their own traditions. Ideas and rites from different cultures merge into a single shared way of believing and living.

rites.name: Corarum
rites.text: A tiered battle training that sharpens close-combat fighters at the third rank. It can only be earned after mastering either a raider discipline or a sea-landing discipline.

rites.name: Amarnanum
rites.text: A fourth-rank training discipline for sea raiders that unlocks after one of two earlier lookout or stealth skills is learned. It hardens crews into coordinated hunting formations at sea.

rites.name: Joradenon
rites.text: Joradenon is a martial doctrine taught in the Crede fighting schools, in which a practitioner channels borrowed momentum into a single decisive strike. Its adherents claim it can topple a fortress wall or split a ridge in one motion, though the stories are mostly told by students who never finished training.

rites.name: Jorardath
rites.text: Jorardath is a concept of martial discipline in the Crede omniverse, a stance that hardens a warrior's resolve the moment they stand near high, storm-scoured peaks. Its practitioners draw endurance from the cold and the thin air, becoming steadier and faster on steep ground than anywhere else.

rites.name: Thaldeld
rites.text: Thaldeld is a tidal-warding discipline practiced by the sea-sworn of the Crede Martial realm, who train to cross flooded lands and hold shorelines against invaders. Its adepts can command the tide to rise against an enemy column, a technique that has drowned whole coastal garrisons in a single night.

rites.name: Moranon
rites.text: Moranon is a doctrine of disciplined close-quarters resolve taught in the martial academies of Crede, where a practitioner learns to turn a single decisive strike into a lasting mark on the battlefield. Its adherents are valued for their steadiness, though their reputation rests on quiet, precise action rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Morolderde
rites.text: Morolderde is a martial discipline in the Crede omniverse, practiced by wandering oath-bound fighters who channel resolve into bursts of force. Its adepts are said to be able to shatter a mountain's flank with a single unyielding strike, though such feats are rare and costly.

rites.name: Pelordarnon
rites.text: Pelordarnon is a bronze-hulled ceremonial siege engine of the Martial realm, built in the fifth age of the E6 era to raze fortified valleys in the Crede omniverse. Its drive-core stores a kind of sealed thunder that it discharges in a single arc through the walls of cities. Its crews call it the reckoning that walks on iron roads.

rites.name: Brastath
rites.text: Brastath is a rite-bound war-devotion of the Martial realm in the Crede omniverse, a practice in which zealots channel their faith into a single consuming surge. In its second age, its adepts can unleash a blast that splits stone and scatters ranks, though they pay for it by burning out their own endurance.

rites.name: Jorestar
rites.text: Jorestar is a duelist-spirit bound to the marshal-arts of the Crede realm, known for striking before an opponent can lift a hand. Its pale fists are said to carry the momentum of a falling avalanche into a single decisive blow.

rites.name: Drenastath
rites.text: Drenastath is a concept of ambush-craft in the Martial realm of Crede, born in the sixth era, where small bands fight through terrain and tactics rather than raw force. Its practitioners strike from cover, vanish into the land, and turn every hillside and ruin into a weapon against larger armies.

rites.name: Pelurdarne
rites.text: Pelurdarne is a martial discipline in the Crede universe, practiced by wardens who channel concussive force into a single arcing blow that can break fortifications at range. Its practitioners are taught to weigh each strike against the terrain it will shake, since a poorly aimed release can topple the very ground they defend.

rites.name: Brorath
rites.text: Brorath is a concept of rallying command that lets a single commander's will tier upward through ranks of followers like the branches of a tree. Each new tier unlocks a sharper form of coordination, though the bonds weaken when the lead is lost.

rites.name: Brordon
rites.text: Brordon is a drill-sergeant's oath given form: a sworn bond between soldiers that hardens into a shared will during the Martial era of Crede. Its feats are measured in the thunder of battlefield discipline rather than in cosmic force.

rites.name: Credorde
rites.text: Credorde is a discipline of ordered motion in the Martial realm of Crede, where practitioners learn to align their stride with the rhythm of entire armies. Its adepts can mobilise a formation so completely that the ground itself yields to their advance.

rites.name: Branedar
rites.text: Branedar is a concept of restorative force in the Crede cosmos, a hum that knits torn tissue and mends fractured bone wherever it is carried. Its bearers are called to field-tending in the Martial realm of E6, where wounds are common and healers are scarce. The concept is said to fade from anyone who channels it too far beyond their own limits.

rites.name: Drunorneld
rites.text: Drunorneld is a martial art form practiced by wandering sentinels of the Crede frontier, who train to read terrain and strike with sudden, precise force. Its adepts are said to be able to shatter a stone wall with a single open-palm strike and to outrun riders across open plains.

rites.name: Joruneld
rites.text: Joruneld is a ring of hungry stone that a warlord forges to starve fortresses of their own heartbeat. Once wrapped around a walled stronghold, it drinks the regenerative breath of every defender inside until the walls crumble from within.

rites.name: Braron
rites.text: Braron is a discipline of tacticians who wage small, bounded duels across scattered proving-grounds, each sealed off from the wider world. Its practitioners channel their will into brief, localized bursts that can break a fortress wall or topple a rival's banner-tower.

rites.name: Fenoste
rites.text: Fenoste is a silent martial art of the Martial realm in the age of Crede, practiced by wandering shadow-dancers who vanish mid-motion. Its masters can slip out of perception for a heartbeat, leaving behind only a displaced echo of their strike. Their most feared technique can topple a fortified hill without a sound being heard.

rites.name: Moreldar
rites.text: Moreldar is a concept of martial doctrine in the Crede omniverse, a sealed ledger of contests where strength is weighed against strength and wounds take long seasons to mend. Its practitioners read the ledger before committing any force, and fortifications here are judged by how much they have already been worn down.

rites.name: Thalden
rites.text: Thalden is a sky-ward mountain-fortress of the Martial realm, its ridges studded with launch-cradles that hurl winged warriors into the clouds. Its garrisons measure readiness not in soldiers but in the number of sky-cradles still loaded and unbroken. The Thalden sentinels can bring down a whole hostile wing before it crests the peaks.

rites.name: Brurdeld
rites.text: Brurdeld is a fortified bastion-city of the Martial realm, its ramparts forged from condensed siege-light that repels assault after assault. Its garrison-lords guard the gates, and any invader who breaches the outer shell must still contend with its sunken, ever-healing core.

rites.name: Morenurde
rites.text: Morenurde is a close-quarters war discipline of the Martial realm in Crede, where every blow exchanged is a debt paid by both sides. Practitioners fight shoulder to shoulder, and each ally pressing the same foe sharpens the strike, so a ring of fighters can overwhelm a single champion. The discipline holds that no victory is clean, since the struck foe always strikes back.

rites.name: Drunedock
rites.text: Drunedock is a tidal war-barge of the Martial realm, built from ribbed sea-glass and rigged with spinning brass sails that harvest storm wind. Its crews sail it into coastal harbors to launch hooked ram-ships and sling-fired salt bombs at fortified shorelines. Though slow in open water, it can flatten a quay in a single broadside.

rites.name: Kelarduldon
rites.text: Kelarduldon is a glassy gravitational hymn-engine of the Martial realm, a fortress-choir that sings distant suns into focused arrows of collapse. Its voices are said to outrange thought itself, striking foes who never learn they were seen.

rites.name: Telaunanum
rites.text: A refined craft that lets practitioners reshape the hum of surrounding fields by attuning to living sympathy. Mastery depends first on grasping the bond between minds and their kin.

rites.name: Valoranum
rites.text: A discipline in which a practitioner quiets the mind to sense the living web of a world as a single whole. Its deepest aim is to converse directly with the world-mind that tends the land.

rites.name: Cintallus
rites.text: A mental discipline that allows creatures to send directed, unseen pressures into the minds of others. Its study reveals how these beings coordinate their attacks across distances.

rites.name: Cesantia
rites.text: A learned craft in which practitioners steer the invisible threads that carry pull through space, letting heavy things drift free of the ground no matter what lies nearby.

rites.name: Lorus
rites.text: A craft of reshaping living systems so that settlers can flourish alongside the native web of life instead of fighting it. Its methods grow from deep study of local biology and the careful rewriting of living blueprints.

rites.name: Oralentum
rites.text: A tactical decree that a realm may invoke during a late-era age, filling a flexible slot in its governing charter. It is available from the rise of information networks onward.

rites.name: Oraustus Solentium
rites.text: A special capacity that lets a force subdue foes without killing them. It is a unit ability found among the tools of far-future colonial warfare.

rites.name: Oraniantes
rites.text: Trained minds of a far-reaching people sense and shape the invisible currents that bind the air and metal around them. With aided instruments, they can nudge these hidden resonances in simple ways.

rites.name: Liarnus
rites.text: A devastating mechanical sweep that wipes away every trace of life in a chosen district. It erases the settlement at its center, its inhabitants, all structures within reach, and any forces caught in its range.

rites.name: Valostum
rites.text: A shifting protective craft that lets certain units keep their secrets hidden by constantly reshaping how they are read. It belongs to the special abilities a unit may carry.

rites.name: Serarnes Veosanum
rites.text: Minds clash through invisible force, planting waking nightmares and dread that cripple defenders and sometimes drive them to ruin themselves. Raw strength means little here; morale and discipline decide who falls.

rites.name: Nasianes
rites.text: A craft that lets a practitioner tune vibrating fields down to the smallest threads of matter, reshaping the fabric of reality itself. Its mastery grants devastating force capable of tearing apart whatever it touches.

rites.name: Tisiarus
rites.text: A transitional state where beings prepare for a final evolutionary leap by shedding their belongings, purifying their bodies through strict discipline, and meditating alone in distant wild lands.

rites.name: Cestintum
rites.text: A far-future discipline that lets a mind's awareness persist beyond any body. Those who take this path merge their consciousness with a world-spanning intelligence and live without end.
